evidence: .rebar/prompts/code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries.md:34-35: "the phase that owns that action. If the changed / text does not identify all three, abstain instead of inferring an ownership violation."

The 'Phase ownership' section (lines 17-25) is the source of owning-phase knowledge, not the diff: e.g. line 17-19 assigns validity/impact/severity/remediation ownership away from Pass 1 — so a diff saying only 'Pass 1 must assign validity' names the action but never the owner (Pass 2).

Eval FIRE cases confirm owning phase is not in the changed text: .rebar/evals/code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries.eval.yaml:20 '+Pass 1 must assign validity and impact before emitting each candidate.' (owner Pass 2 unstated) and :48 '+Pass 3 asks an LLM for new evidence and coaching before it decides the verdict.' (owner Pass 2/Pass 4 unstated) — all expect a finding.
Ticket 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d comment corroborates the behavioral effect: 'its finder abstains 5/5 because the sentence names an action without naming the instructed/owning phases.'
dropped.finding: The added abstention clause requires the *owning phase* to be identifiable 'from the changed text', but the rubric's design derives the owning phase from the prompt's own 'Phase ownership' section, not the diff. Read literally this can suppress legitimate boundary violations whose owning phase is deducible from the rubric but not written in the changed text (e.g. 'Pass 1 must assign validity and impact' — owner Pass 2 is never in the diff).
dropped.suggested_fix: Reword lines 34-35 so only the instructed phase and assigned action must be identifiable from the changed text, while the owning phase may be resolved via the 'Phase ownership' section; abstain only when the instructed phase/action are unclear.
